name: Ranger TaelcwÝR
body:
Note: This archetype is designed for elves, but may be taken by members of other species with the GM’s permission.

Among some groups of elves, taelcwýrs are considered to be the ultimate guardians of the people. Dedicated equally to the preservation of knowledge, harmony with nature, and the protection of elven society, taelcwýrs are few in number and often solitary in existence. They choose their allies and their missions carefully, often spending decades between adventures as they pore over tomes of lore or dedicate their time serving as peacetime ambassadors.

Researched Enemy

The bonus you gain from the favored enemy class feature does not apply to Bluff or Sense Motive checks, but does apply to and Spellcraft checks. In addition, Knowledge (arcana) is a class skill for you. This feature alters class skills and favored enemy.

Divine Spells

Beginning at 4th level, you gain the ability to cast a small number of divine spells, which are drawn from the druid spell list, except that only druid spells up to 3rd level are considered to be on your spell list. You must choose and prepare your spells in advance. Like a druid, you can cast any summon nature’s ally spell spontaneously in place of a prepared spell of the same level or lower.

To prepare or cast a divine spell, you must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against one of your divine spells is 10 + the spell level + your Wisdom modifier.

Like other spellcasters, you can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Your base daily allotment of divine spells is given on Table 2–1: Divine Spells per Day, above. In addition, you receive bonus divine spells per day if you have a high Wisdom score. When Table 2–1 indicates that you get 0 spells per day of a given spell level, you gain only the bonus spells you would be entitled to based on your Wisdom score for that spell level.

You must spend 1 hour per day in quiet meditation to regain your daily allotment of spells. You may prepare and cast any spell on your divine spell list, provided that you can cast spells of that level, but you must choose which spells to prepare during your daily meditation.

Through 3rd level, you have no caster level.

At 4th level and higher, your caster level is equal to your ranger level –3. This feature alters the ranger’s spells.

Arcane Spells And Cantrips

Beginning at 4th level, you can prepare a number of cantrips, or arcane 0-level spells, each day, as noted on Table 2–2: Arcane Spells per Day. (Cantrips are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.) At 7th level, you gain the ability to cast a small number of spells, except that only sorcerer/wizard spells up to 3rd level are considered to be on your spell list. Your cantrips and other arcane spells are drawn from the sorcerer/wizard spell list.

To learn, prepare, or cast an arcane spell, you must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against one of your arcane spells is 10 + the spell level + your Intelligence modifier.

Your base daily allotment of arcane spells is given on Table 2–2. In addition, you receive bonus arcane spells per day if you have a high Intelligence score. When Table 2–2 indicates that you get 0 spells per day of a given spell level, you gain only the bonus spells you would be entitled to based on your Intelligence score for that spell level.

You may know any number of arcane spells.

You must choose and prepare your spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying your spellbook. While studying, you decide which spells to prepare. This may be done while you meditate for your divine spells.

You can cast your arcane ranger spells while wearing light or medium armor and using a shield without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. This feature replaces hunter’s bond.
